transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-15
Start: 10:30 AM PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom / internal training room
Attendees: Jordan Reyes, Priya Nair, Ethan Liu, Maya Chen, Sofia Patel, Carlos Mendes, Leila Noor, Tom Brooks

Summary: Short, focused SE enablement session: 45 minute rehearsal of hosted vs dedicated messaging, three short demo runs (prompt engineering + streaming demo), and a 10 minute open Q&A on competitive positioning. Actionable next steps taken at the end.

Topics covered: Messaging pillars (cost/latency/reliability), demo script order, fallback and routing story, dedicated vs hosted pitch for regulated customers, handling Bedrock & Anthropic objections, and live role-play of onboarding flow.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Alright everyone, welcome. This is the SE sprint, we'll run through messaging quick, then do two recorded demos and a roleplay. Trying to keep it tight.
[00:18] Priya: Hey all, hi, I'm Priya SE — I'll run the demo parts and try the streaming example twice, once with default batching and once with prefix caching.
[00:30] Sofia: Thanks Jordan, thanks Priya. Quick note - Oakbridge cares a lot about data residency and KMS keys, so we'll want concrete lines on Private/VPC.
[00:44] Jordan: Absolutely, good call. We'll show the Private deployment bullets and the KMS integration slide during the pitch.
[00:52] Tom: Also want to see how Dedicated pools handle burst vs reserved throughput, real numbers are helpful.
[01:04] Priya: I have those numbers, approximate QPS for a p4-like node and an A100 cluster; I'll make sure they're in the script. Note, numbers are tuned per model and quantization.
[01:18] Ethan: Quick note on competitive positioning—when Anthropic comes up we lean into our throughput and fallback story; when Bedrock/AWS comes up we emphasize unified API and predictable unit economics.
[01:35] Carlos: Mm-hmm. How do you position pricing against OpenAI though? We get asked some sticker shock questions.
[01:44] Maya: Two angles: 1) per-unit TCO including autoscale and caching, 2) reliability and SLOs for production. Practically we show a sample cost calc comparing per-token rates + KV cache savings.
[01:58] Jordan: Great. Ok demo one: live chat streaming with function calling turned on. Priya you'll start, try to hit the routing fallback scenario by simulating a model OOM.
[02:12] Priya: Copy. Sharing screen... (audio glitch) sorry, let me reshare.
[02:25] [02:25] Priya: Starting demo - prompt: 'Summarize quarterly ops notes and extract action items, highlight regulatory flags'... streaming response starts...
[02:40] Priya: So here you can see streaming chunks, there's a 180ms average client-side latency shown — in hosted we often see 70-120ms per chunk depending on region.
[02:54] Sofia: That number's useful; can you also show the token-level cost break down?
[03:06] Priya: Yep, pulling up the console cost view — here it's broken down by prompt vs generation tokens and the KV cache hits. Note: numbers are illustrative.
[03:20] [03:20] Jordan: Roleplay interjection: Pretend you're an exec who cares only about cost. Priya you reframe the story in 30 seconds.
[03:30] Priya: Sure — we focus on two levers: caching and batching. Show how prefix caching can reduce repeated prompt cost by up to 60% for templated workflows, and batching smooths your p99 latency at high concurrency.
[03:45] [03:45] Carlos: Quick interruption, what about model updates? We need version pinning for audits.
[03:51] Priya: Good point — show model catalog and version pin. Also can do canary rollouts with automatic fallback to previous pinned model if regressions detected.
[04:05] Ethan: Add that we integrate with customers' eval suites; Quality Monitoring ties directly to rollouts so we can block bad updates.
[04:16] [04:16] Demo glitch: screen lags a bit while switching to Dedicated config.
[04:30] Priya: Switching to Dedicated config: here's the same request hitting a dedicated pool, you can see lower jitter and stable p50/p99 numbers.
[04:48] Tom: Are these numbers from real benchmarks? Might want to caveat — customers push back if it's purely synthetic.
[04:56] Jordan: We'll note 'benchmarks run on representative workload' and attach spreadsheet; send the raw CSV if asked.
[05:10] [05:10] Jordan: Good practice point: When prospect asks for 'benchmarks', ask about sequence length distribution, concurrency pattern, and the model family — we need those to reproduce numbers.
[05:27] Priya: Demo two: show fallback routing — intentionally throttle the dedicated pool to force routing to hosted compatible variant.
[05:40] [05:40] Priya: Triggering throttle... fallback fires... new model variant picked... response returns. You can see a small increase in latency but no errors for the user.
[05:57] Sofia: This is exactly the resilience story we want to hear for enterprise. How is data handled during fallback, is anything sent to different tenancy?
[06:08] Priya: No, policy can enforce same tenancy; fallback can be to a compatible model within the same deployment plane, or to hosted with explicit consent and logging. We'll highlight the audit trail in the console.
[06:25] Jordan: Quick pivot — competitive role-play. Samir will be 'customer buyer', Maya you'll play 'Anthropic rep' — let's rehearse answers to the 'we already use Anthropic for alignment' objection.
[06:40] Samir: (in a mock stern buyer voice) We like Anthropic for safety — why would we move?
[06:48] Maya (as Anthropic): We have pre-tuned safety systems—
[06:52] Priya (jumping in): Acknowledge their safety investments, then pivot: Redwood isn't trying to replace model-level safety, we offer serving controls, predictable latency and the ability to do private deployments with your own governance. Combine model safety with our serving guarantees.
[07:12] [07:12] Jordan: Good, call out the 'combine' language — that's a repeatable sentence.
[07:20] Carlos: Does Redwood support in-house fine-tuning or RLHF pipelines?
[07:29] Ethan: Short answer: we integrate with customer fine-tuning pipelines; we host model variants and support model artifacts, but we don't provide RLHF tooling as a managed service — we integrate into your infra for that.
[07:45] [07:45] Jordan: Primer on procurement Qs: be ready to show SOC2/ISO statements, SSO/SAML diagrams, data retention windows and KMS details.
[07:59] Leila: And the integration timeline — how long to get a Private VPC up?
[08:07] Priya: Typical internal timeline is 6-8 weeks for VPC + KMS onboarding for a medium enterprise, shorter if they accept hosted + dedicated hybrid. We'll add the timeline slide.
[08:20] [08:20] Demo three: quick prompt optimization example — show token savings when moving from verbose prompts to structured system messages.
[08:35] Priya: Starting... Here the original prompt is 340 tokens, with structured system + function schema it's 120 tokens and the same quality is preserved.
[08:50] Tom: Nice visual. Can we get a before/after CSV for cost talkbacks?
[08:58] Jordan: Yes, attach the cost calc in the follow-up.
[09:05] [09:05] Roleplay: objection - 'We're worried about vendor lock-in'
[09:12] Priya: Answer: Support open model families, exportable model artifacts, and standard APIs — customers can move to self-hosted variants or other providers; Redwood is an orchestration layer. Emphasize migration playbooks.
[09:30] [09:30] Jordan: Time check - ten more minutes, let's do rapid-fire questions.
[09:36] Carlos: Two quick things: 1) Does Redwood support GPU isolation per tenant? 2) How do you handle KV cache purge requests?
[09:46] Priya: 1) Yes on Dedicated we drive tenancy isolation; 2) KV purge is an API call and we emit an audit log event.
[09:55] [09:55] Sofia: Do you support per-route quotas and custom throttling policies?
[10:02] Maya: Yes, per-route quotas, token caps and soft/hard throttles. Demo available.
[10:10] [10:10] Jordan: Last mock demo: 4-min condensed executive pitch. Priya you're on stage, sell Redwood in 90 seconds to a CFO.
[10:20] Priya: (concise) Redwood Inference reduces per-unit inference cost through caching and smart routing, preserves latency SLOs through dedicated pools and autoscale, and lowers risk by providing private deployment and auditability. Customers see predictable spend and operational simplicity compared to building in-house.
[10:40] [10:40] Samir: Good. One nit: add a quick ROI line with a sample percent reduction for templated workflows.
[10:47] Jordan: Noted. Ok wrap-up — quick recap of next steps and owners.
[10:55] Priya: I'll update demo deck and push to shared link: https://redwood.internal/shared/demo-decks/se-sprint-july15 (note: internal link).
[11:05] Jordan: I'll draft the competitor one-pager and circulate. Carlos/Oakbridge will send sample prompts. We'll set up the follow-up mock demo — proposed date 2025-07-29.
[11:18] Sofia: Thanks all, this was useful.
[11:22] Jordan: Thanks team, session adjourned.

--- End Transcript ---
